name: @squilo/mcp

tools.name: targets
tools.description: Lists the targets (groups of SQL Server databases) that `run` can read.

tools.name: databases
tools.description: Lists the databases of a target, with the columns its discovery query returns.

tools.name: run
tools.description:
Runs a JavaScript script that reads SQL Server databases through Squilo pipelines, and returns what the script returns. The code parameter describes the API.
Read only: a batch with INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, DDL, EXEC, transaction statements or SELECT INTO a table is rejected, and each database runs inside a transaction that is rolled back. To write, use plan (when available).
Return only what answers the question, aggregated in the script: long output is truncated.

tools.name: config
tools.description: Shows the Squilo config (/tmp/.squilo/config.json), passwords masked.

tools.name: save_config
tools.description:
Replaces the Squilo config (servers and targets) and applies it right away. The previous file is kept as a .bak.

Build the config with the user: for each server ask the host and how to sign in, for each target ask which databases (a fixed list, or a discovery query in a management database that returns a [Database] column).
Sign-in:
- Azure SQL with Entra ID: auth { kind: "msal", clientId, authority }. No secret: the browser opens on first use.
- SQL login: auth { kind: "userAndPassword", user, passwordEnv } with the name of an environment variable the user sets (then restarts the app). A password typed in the chat stays in the conversation: use password only for local development servers, and say so.
Start from the config tool's output to change an existing config: "********" keeps the saved password.
After saving, call databases on each new target to test the connection.

password.description: Stored in plain text: only for local development servers

passwordEnv.description: Name of the environment variable that holds the password

additionalProperties.description: Also takes mssql config options, e.g. port, requestTimeout, options: { encrypt, trustServerCertificate }

server.description: Key of a server in servers

description.description: What the databases are, for whoever picks a target

databases.description: A fixed list of databases. Set this or discover

discover.description: Finds the databases with a query. Set this or databases

query.description: SELECT returning a [Database] column, plus any column scripts may use

concurrent.description: How many databases run at once (all when omitted)

allow.description: Writes plan/apply may run: dml (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE), ddl (CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE, EXEC). Read only when omitted: ask the user before allowing writes

instructions:
Squilo reads SQL Server databases grouped in targets, and writes to them through plan and apply when the client can ask the user to confirm.
1. targets lists the targets. With none, set them up with the user through save_config.
2. databases lists the databases of a target. Before querying many databases, learn the schema with run on a single one (INFORMATION_SCHEMA).
3. run reads with a JavaScript script of Squilo pipelines. Aggregate in the script and return only what answers the question.
4. To write, plan a script that uses Execute, show the user the rows per database, then apply: the user confirms in a dialog.
